sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%无形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Morris.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·莫里斯。

sentences.en: On April 9th, 2017, United Airlines Flight 3411 was about to fly from Chicago to Louisville
sentences.zh: 2017年4月9日，美联航3411号航班正准备从芝加哥飞往路易斯维尔

sentences.en: when flight attendants discovered the plane was overbooked.
sentences.zh: 当时乘务员发现飞机超售了。

sentences.en: They tried to get volunteers to give up their seats with promises of travel vouchers and hotel accommodations,
sentences.zh: 他们试图通过承诺提供旅行代金券和酒店住宿来寻找自愿放弃座位的乘客，

sentences.en: but not enough people were willing to get off.
sentences.zh: 但没有足够的人愿意下机。

sentences.en: United ended up calling some airport security officers.
sentences.zh: 美联航最终叫来了几名机场保安人员。

sentences.en: They boarded the plane and forcibly removed a passenger named Dr. David Dow.
sentences.zh: 他们登上飞机，强行拖拽了一名叫大卫·道（David Dow）博士的乘客。

sentences.en: The officers ripped Dow out of his seat and carried him down the aisle on the airplane,
sentences.zh: 保安人员将道博士从座位上强行扯下来，并把他沿着飞机的过道拖走，

sentences.en: nose bleeding, while horrified onlookers shot video with their phones.
sentences.zh: 当时他鼻青脸肿、流着血，而惊恐的围观者则用手机拍摄了视频。

sentences.en: You probably remember this incident and the outrage it generated.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得这起事件以及它所引发的愤怒。

sentences.en: The international uproar continued over the forced removal of a passenger from a United Airlines flight.
sentences.zh: 由于美联航航班上发生乘客被强行驱离事件，国际上的抗议声浪持续不断。

sentences.en: Today, the airline's CEO, Oscar Munoz, issued an apology, saying, quote,
sentences.zh: 今天，该航空公司首席执行官奥斯卡·穆诺斯（Oscar Munoz）发表道歉声明，原话如下：

sentences.en: no one should ever be mistreated this way.
sentences.zh: 任何人都不应受到这种方式的虐待。

sentences.en: I want you to know that we take full responsibility and we will work.
sentences.zh: 我想让你们知道，我们承担全部责任，我们将采取行动。

sentences.en: But why Dr. Dow?
sentences.zh: 但为什么偏偏是道博士？

sentences.en: How did he end up being the unlucky passenger that United decided to remove?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么成为美联航决定驱逐的不幸乘客的？

sentences.en: Immediately following the incident, some people thought racial discrimination may have played a part,
sentences.zh: 事件发生后不久，一些人认为种族歧视可能在其中起了一定作用，

sentences.en: and it's possible that this played a role in how he was treated.
sentences.zh: 并且这有可能对他的遭遇产生了一定影响。

sentences.en: But the answer to how he was chosen was actually an algorithm, a computer program.
sentences.zh: 但关于他是如何被选中的，答案其实是一个算法，一个计算机程序。

sentences.en: It crunched through a bunch of data, looking at stuff like how much each passenger had paid for their ticket,
sentences.zh: 它处理了大量数据，考察诸如每位乘客为机票支付了多少钱、

sentences.en: what time they checked in, how often they flew on United, and whether they were part of a rewards program.
sentences.zh: 他们是什么时候办理登机手续的、他们乘坐美联航飞机的频率如何，以及他们是否加入了奖励计划。

sentences.en: The algorithm likely determined that Dr. Dow was one of the least valuable customers on the flight at the time.
sentences.zh: 该算法很可能判定道博士是当时航班上价值最低的乘客之一。

sentences.en: Algorithms shape our world in profound and mostly invisible ways.
sentences.zh: 算法以深远且大多无形的方式塑造着我们的世界。

sentences.en: They predict if we'll be valuable customers or whether we're likely to repay a loan.
sentences.zh: 它们预测我们会成为有价值的客户，还是可能会偿还贷款。

sentences.en: They filter what we see on social media, sort through resumes, and evaluate job performance.
sentences.zh: 它们过滤我们在社交媒体上看到的内容，筛选简历，并评估工作绩效。

sentences.en: They inform prison sentences and monitor our health.
sentences.zh: 它们为量刑提供参考并监测我们的健康状况。

sentences.en: Most of these algorithms have been created with good intentions.
sentences.zh: 这些算法大多数都是出于好意而创建的。

sentences.en: The goal is to replace subjective judgments with objective measurements.
sentences.zh: 其目标是用客观的测量来取代主观的判断。

sentences.en: But it doesn't always work out like that.
sentences.zh: 但事情并不总是如愿以偿。

sentences.en: This subject is huge.
sentences.zh: 这个课题非常庞大。

sentences.en: I think algorithm design may be the big design problem of the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 我认为算法设计可能是21世纪最大的设计问题。

sentences.en: And that's why I wanted to interview Kathy O'Neill.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我想采访凯西·奥尼尔（Kathy O'Neill）。

sentences.en: Okay, well, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢。

sentences.en: So can we start, can you give me one of them sort of NPR-style introductions and just say your name and what you do?
sentences.zh: 那么我们可以开始吗？你能给我一个那种NPR风格的介绍，说出你的名字和你的工作吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I'm Kathy O'Neill.
sentences.zh: 我是凯西·奥尼尔。

sentences.en: I'm a mathematician, data scientist, activist, and author.
sentences.zh: 我是一名数学家、数据科学家、活动家和作家。

sentences.en: I wrote the book, Weapons of Math Destruction, How Big Data Increases Inequality and Threatens Democracy.
sentences.zh: 我写过一本书：《数学破坏武器：大数据如何加剧不平等并威胁民主》。

sentences.en: O'Neill studied number theory and then left academia to build predictive algorithms for a hedge fund.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔曾研究数论，后来离开学术界，为一家对冲基金构建预测算法。

sentences.en: But she got really disillusioned by the use of mathematical models in the financial industry.
sentences.zh: 但她对金融行业中数学模型的使用彻底幻灭了。

sentences.en: I wanted to, like, have more impact in the world.
sentences.zh: 我想，在世界上产生更大的影响。

sentences.en: But I didn't really know that that impact could be really terrible.
sentences.zh: 但我并不知道这种影响可能会变得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I was very naive.
sentences.zh: 我当时非常天真。

sentences.en: After that, O'Neill worked as a data scientist at a couple of startups.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，奥尼尔在几家初创公司担任数据科学家。

sentences.en: And through these experiences, she started to get worried about the influence of poorly designed algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 通过这些经历，她开始对设计糟糕的算法的影响感到担忧。

sentences.en: So we'll start with the most obvious question.
sentences.zh: 那么我们从最明显的问题开始。

sentences.en: What is an algorithm?
sentences.zh: 什么是算法？

sentences.en: At its most basic, an algorithm is a step-by-step guide to solving a problem.
sentences.zh: 最基础地说，算法是解决问题的分步指南。

sentences.en: It's a set of instructions, like a recipe.
sentences.zh: 它是一组指令，就像食谱一样。

sentences.en: The example I like to give is, like, cooking dinner for my family.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢举的例子是，为我的家人做晚饭。

sentences.en: So in this case, the problem is how to make a successful dinner.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，问题是如何做出成功的晚餐。

sentences.en: O'Neill starts with a set of ingredients.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔从一组食材开始。

sentences.en: And as she's creating the meal, she's constantly making choices about what ingredients are healthy enough to include in her dinner algorithm.
sentences.zh: 在她制作这顿饭的过程中，她不断地做出选择，决定哪些食材健康到足以纳入她的晚餐算法中。

sentences.en: I curate that data because those ramen noodle packages that my kids like so much, I don't think of those as ingredients, right?
sentences.zh: 我策划那些数据，因为我孩子们非常喜欢的那些拉面包装，我不认为它们是食材，对吧？

sentences.en: So I exclude them.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它们排除了。

sentences.en: I'm curating.
sentences.zh: 我在策划。

sentences.en: And I'm therefore imposing my agenda on this algorithm.
sentences.zh: 因此，我将我的议程强加到了这个算法上。

sentences.en: In addition to curating the ingredients, O'Neill, as the cook, also defines what a successful outcome looks like.
sentences.zh: 除了策划食材，奥尼尔作为厨师，还定义了成功的标准是什么。

sentences.en: I'm also defining success, right?
sentences.zh: 我还在定义成功，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm in charge of success.
sentences.zh: 我掌控着成功。

sentences.en: I define success to be if my kids eat vegetables at that meal.
sentences.zh: 我将成功定义为我的孩子们在那顿饭里吃了蔬菜。

sentences.en: And, you know, a different cook might define success differently.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，不同的厨师可能会对成功有不同的定义。

sentences.en: You know, my eight-year-old would define success to be, like, whether he got to eat Nutella.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我八岁的孩子会把成功定义为他是否能吃上能多益（Nutella）。

sentences.en: So that's another way where we, the builders, impose our agenda on the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们这些构建者将我们的议程强加给算法的另一种方式。

sentences.en: O'Neill's main point here is that algorithms aren't really objective, even when they're carried out by computers.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔这里的核心观点是，算法其实并不是客观的，即使它们是由计算机执行的。

sentences.en: This is relevant because the companies that build them like to market them as objective, claiming they remove human error and fallibility from complex decision-making.
sentences.zh: 这一点之所以重要，是因为构建它们的喜欢将它们作为客观事物进行营销，声称它们从复杂的决策中消除了人为错误和不可靠性。

sentences.en: But every algorithm reflects the priorities and judgments of its human designer.
sentences.zh: 但每一个算法都反映了其人类设计者的优先级和判断。

sentences.en: Of course, that doesn't necessarily make algorithms bad.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不一定意味着算法是坏的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's very important to me that I don't get the reputation of hating all algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，对我来说非常重要的是，我不要落得一个讨厌所有算法的名声。

sentences.en: I actually like algorithms, and I think algorithms could really help.
sentences.zh: 我其实喜欢算法，而且我认为算法真的可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: But O'Neill does single out a particular kind of algorithm for scrutiny.
sentences.zh: 但奥尼尔确实挑出了一种特定类型的算法来进行审视。

sentences.en: These are the ones we should worry about.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我们应该担心的。

sentences.en: And they're characterized by three properties, that they're very widespread and important.
sentences.zh: 它们的特征有三个属性，即它们非常普遍且重要。

sentences.en: So, like, they make important decisions about a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如，它们对很多人做出重要的决定。

sentences.en: Number two, that they're secret, that the people don't understand how they're being scored.
sentences.zh: 第二，它们是秘密的，人们并不了解自己是如何被评分的。

sentences.en: And number three, that they're destructive.
sentences.zh: 第三，它们具有破坏性。

sentences.en: Like, one bad mistake in the design, if you will, of these algorithms will actually not only make it unfair for individuals,
sentences.zh: 比如，这些算法设计中的一个错误，如果你愿意这么说的话，实际上不仅会对个人造成不公平，

sentences.en: but sort of categorically unfair for enormous populations as it gets scaled up.
sentences.zh: 而且随着规模扩大，会对庞大的人群造成绝对的不公平。

sentences.en: O'Neill has a shorthand for these algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔对这些算法有一个简称。

sentences.en: The widespread, mysterious, and destructive ones.
sentences.zh: 那些广泛存在、神秘莫测且具有破坏性的算法。

sentences.en: She calls them weapons of math destruction.
sentences.zh: 她称它们为数学破坏武器。

sentences.en: To show how one of these destructive algorithms works, O'Neill points to the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 为了展示其中一个破坏性算法是如何运作的，奥尼尔指出了刑事司法系统。

sentences.en: For hundreds of years, key decisions in the legal process, like the amount of bail, length of sentence, and likelihood of parole,
sentences.zh: 几百年来，法律程序中的关键决定，比如保释金金额、刑期长短和假释可能性，

sentences.en: have been in the hands of fallible human beings guided by their instincts, and sometimes their personal biases.
sentences.zh: 一直掌握在易犯错误的人类手中，他们受直觉引导，有时也受个人偏见支配。

sentences.en: The judges are sort of famously racist, some of them more than others.
sentences.zh: 法官们在某种程度上以种族主义闻名，其中一些人比其他人更严重。

sentences.en: And that racism can produce very different outcomes for defendants.
sentences.zh: 这种种族主义会给被告带来截然不同的结果。

sentences.en: For example, the ACLU has found that sentences imposed on black men in the federal system are nearly 20% longer than those for white men convicted of similar crimes.
sentences.zh: 例如，美国公民自由联盟（ACLU）发现，在联邦系统中对黑人男性判处的主刑比因类似罪行被定罪的白人男性长近20%。

sentences.en: And studies have shown that prosecutors are more likely to seek the death penalty for African Americans than for whites convicted of the same charges.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，与因相同罪名被定罪的白人相比，检察官更有可能对非裔美国人寻求死刑。

sentences.en: So you might think that computerized models fed by data would contribute to more even-handed treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会认为，由数据喂养的计算机模型将有助于更公正的对待。

sentences.en: The criminal justice system thinks so too.
sentences.zh: 刑事司法系统也是这么认为的。

sentences.en: It has increasingly tried to minimize human bias by turning to risk assessment algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 它越来越多地试图通过转向风险评估算法来最小化人类偏见。

sentences.en: Like crime risk, like what is the chance of someone coming back to prison after leaving it?
sentences.zh: 像犯罪风险，比如某人在离开监狱后再次入狱几率是多少？

sentences.en: Many of these risk algorithms look at a person's record of arrests and convictions.
sentences.zh: 许多这样的风险算法会查看一个人的逮捕和定罪记录。

sentences.en: The problem is, that data is already skewed by some social realities.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这些数据已经被一些社会现实扭曲了。

sentences.en: Take, for example, the fact that white people and black people use marijuana at roughly equal rates.
sentences.zh: 以白人和黑人吸食大麻的比例大致相当这一事实为例。

sentences.en: And yet...
sentences.zh: 然而……

sentences.en: There's five times as many blacks getting arrested for smoking pot as whites.
sentences.zh: 因吸大麻而被捕的黑人人数是白人的五倍。

sentences.en: Five times as many.
sentences.zh: 整整五倍。

sentences.en: This may be because black neighborhoods tend to be more heavily policed than white neighborhoods,
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为黑人社区往往比白人社区受到更严密的巡逻，

sentences.en: which means black people get arrested for certain crimes more often than white people.
sentences.zh: 这意味着黑人比白人更频繁地因某些罪行而被捕。

sentences.en: Risk algorithms detect these patterns and apply them to the future.
sentences.zh: 风险算法检测到这些模式并将它们应用到未来。

sentences.en: So if the past is shaped in part by racism, the future will be too.
sentences.zh: 所以如果过去部分由种族主义塑造，未来也将会如此。

sentences.en: The larger point is, we have terrible data here.
sentences.zh: 更广泛的观点是，我们这里有糟糕的数据。

sentences.en: But the statisticians involved, the data scientists, are like blithely going forward and pretending that our data is good.
sentences.zh: 但涉及的统计学家、数据科学家却在无忧无虑地前进，假装我们的数据很好。

sentences.en: And then we're using it to actually make important decisions.
sentences.zh: 然后我们用它来实际做出重要决定。

sentences.en: Risk assessment algorithms also look at defendants' answers to a questionnaire that's supposed to tease out certain risk factors.
sentences.zh: 风险评估算法还会查看被告对旨在探究某些风险因素的问卷的回答。

sentences.en: They have questions like, you know, did you grow up in a high crime neighborhood?
sentences.zh: 他们有一些问题，比如，你是在高犯罪率社区长大的吗？

sentences.en: Are you on welfare?
sentences.zh: 你在领救济金吗？

sentences.en: Do you have a mental health problem?
sentences.zh: 你有心理健康问题吗？

sentences.en: Do you have addiction problems?
sentences.zh: 你有瘾癖问题吗？

sentences.en: Did your father go to prison?
sentences.zh: 你父亲进过监狱吗？

sentences.en: You know, they're basically proxies for race and class.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们基本上是种族和阶级的替代指标。

sentences.en: But it's embedded in this scoring system.
sentences.zh: 但它被嵌入到这个评分系统中。

sentences.en: And the judge is given the score and it's called objective.
sentences.zh: 法官得到了分数，并且这被称为客观。

sentences.en: What does a judge take away from it or, you know, how is it used?
sentences.zh: 法官从中得到了什么，或者说，它是如何被使用的？

sentences.en: If you have a high risk score, it's used to send you to prison for longer in sentencing.
sentences.zh: 如果你有高风险评分，它在判刑时会被用来把你送进监狱更长时间。

sentences.en: There's also, it's also used in bail hearings and parole hearings.
sentences.zh: 还有，它也被用在保释听证会和假释听证会上。

sentences.en: If you have a high recidivism risk score, you don't get parole.
sentences.zh: 如果你有很高的累犯风险评分，你就得不到假释。

sentences.en: And presumably you could take all that biased input data and say, this high chance of recidivism means that we should rehabilitate more.
sentences.zh: 据推测，你可以拿所有这些有偏见的输入数据说，这很高的累犯几率意味着我们应该进行更多康复工作。

sentences.en: I mean, you could take all that same stuff and choose to do a completely different thing with the result of the algorithm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以拿所有这些相同的东西，选择对算法的结果做一件完全不同的事情。

sentences.en: That's exactly my point.
sentences.zh: 这正是我的观点。

sentences.en: Exactly my point.
sentences.zh: 这正是我的观点。

sentences.en: You know, we could say, oh, I wonder why people who have this characteristic have so much worse recidivism.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们可以说，哦，我很好奇为什么具有这种特征的人有高得多的累犯率。

sentences.en: Well, let's try to help them find a job.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们试着帮他们找一份工作。

sentences.en: Maybe that'll help.
sentences.zh: 也许那会有帮助。

sentences.en: We could use those algorithms, those risk scores to try to account for our society.
sentences.zh: 我们可以利用那些算法、那些风险评分来试着正视我们的社会。

sentences.en: Instead, O'Neill says, in many cases, we're effectively penalizing people for societal and structural issues that they have little control over.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔说，相反，在许多情况下，我们实际上是在因他们几乎无法控制的社会和结构问题而惩罚人们。

sentences.en: And we're doing it at a massive scale using these new technological tools.
sentences.zh: 而且我们正在使用这些新技术工具大规模地这样做。

sentences.en: We're shifting the blame, if you will, from the society, which is the one that should own these problems, to the individual and punishing them for it.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意这么说的话，我们正在将责任从本应承担这些问题的社会转移到个人身上，并因此惩罚他们。

sentences.en: It should be said that in some cases, algorithms are helping to change elements of the criminal justice system for the better.
sentences.zh: 必须指出的是，在某些情况下，算法正在帮助改变刑事司法系统的某些要素使其变得更好。

sentences.en: For example, New Jersey recently did away with their cash bail system, which disadvantaged low-income defendants.
sentences.zh: 例如，新泽西州最近废除了现金保释制度，该制度对低收入被告不利。

sentences.en: They now rely on predictive algorithms instead.
sentences.zh: 他们现在转而依赖预测算法。

sentences.en: Data shows that the state's pre-trial county jail populations are down by about 20%.
sentences.zh: 数据显示，该州审前县监狱的人数下降了约20%。

sentences.en: But still, algorithms like that one remain unaudited and unregulated.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，像那样的算法仍然未经审计且不受监管。

sentences.en: And it's a problem when algorithms are basically black boxes.
sentences.zh: 当算法基本上是黑箱时，这就是个问题。

sentences.en: In many cases, they're designed by private companies who sell them to other companies.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，它们是由将它们出售给其他公司的私营公司设计的。

sentences.en: And the exact details of how they work aren't kept secret.
sentences.zh: 它们工作原理的具体细节并没有被保密。

sentences.en: Not only is the public in the dark, even the companies using these things might not understand exactly how the data is being processed.
sentences.zh: 不仅公众被蒙在鼓里，甚至使用这些东西的公司可能也不完全理解数据是如何被处理的。

sentences.en: This is true of many of the problematic algorithms that O'Neill has looked at, whether they're used for sorting loan applications or assessing teacher performance.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔研究过的许多有问题算法都是如此，无论是用于筛选贷款申请还是评估教师绩效。

sentences.en: There's some kind of weird thing that happens to people when mathematical scores are trotted out.
sentences.zh: 当数学分数被拿出来时，人们身上会发生某种奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: They just start closing their eyes and believing it because it's math.
sentences.zh: 他们只是开始闭上眼睛并相信它，因为那是数学。

sentences.en: And I feel like, oh, I'm not an expert of math, so I can't push back.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，哦，我不是数学专家，所以我无法反击。

sentences.en: And that's something you just see time and time again.
sentences.zh: 那是你一次又一次看到的事情。

sentences.en: You're like, why didn't you question this?
sentences.zh: 你会想，你为什么不质疑这个？

sentences.en: This doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这说不通。

sentences.en: Oh, well, it's math and I don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，这是数学，我听不懂。

sentences.en: Right now, it seems like because of algorithms and math, it's just a new place to place blame so that you do not have to think about your decisions as an actual company.
sentences.zh: 现在，由于算法和数学，似乎这只是一个推卸责任的新地方，这样你就不用以一家实际公司的身份去思考你的决定了。

sentences.en: Because these things are just so powerful and so, you know, mesmerizing to us, especially right now, they can be used in all kinds of nefarious ways.
sentences.zh: 因为这些东西对我们来说太强大了，而且太令人着迷了，尤其是现在，它们可以被用于各种各样的恶劣方式。

sentences.en: They're almost magical.
sentences.zh: 它们简直像有魔法一样。

sentences.en: Is that, yeah, that's scary.
sentences.zh: 那是，对，这挺可怕的。

sentences.en: It's scary, and I think I would go one step further than that.
sentences.zh: 这很可怕，而且我觉得我的看法比这还要深入一层。

sentences.en: I feel like, just by observation, that these algorithms, they don't show up randomly.
sentences.zh: 我感觉，仅仅通过观察就能发现，这些算法并不是随机出现的。

sentences.en: They show up when there's a really difficult conversation that people want to avoid.
sentences.zh: 它们出现在人们想要回避一些真正艰难的对话时。

sentences.en: They're like, oh, we don't know what makes a good teacher, and different people have different opinions about that.
sentences.zh: 它们就像是在说，哦，我们不知道什么样才算好老师，不同的人对此有不同的看法。

sentences.en: So let's just bypass this conversation by having an algorithm score teachers.
sentences.zh: 所以，干脆让算法来给老师打分，以此绕过这个讨论吧。

sentences.en: Or we don't know what prison is really for.
sentences.zh: 或者我们根本不知道监狱到底是用来干什么的。

sentences.en: You know, let's have a way of deciding how long to sentence somebody.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们就想出个办法来决定判某人多少年刑。

sentences.en: We introduce these silver bullet mathematical algorithms because we don't want to have a conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们引入了这些号称能解决一切问题的数学算法，因为我们不想去进行对话。

sentences.en: In O'Neill's book, she writes about this young guy named Kyle Beam who takes some time off college to get treated for bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 在奥尼尔的书里，她写到了一个叫凯尔·比姆的年轻小伙子，他休学一段时间去治疗双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: Once he's better and ready to go back to school, he applies for a part-time job at Kroger, which is a big grocery store chain.
sentences.zh: 等他康复并准备重返学校时，他申请了克罗格的一份兼职工作，克罗格是一家大型连锁超市。

sentences.en: He has a friend who works there who offers to vouch for him.
sentences.zh: 他有一个在那儿工作的朋友主动提出为他担保。

sentences.en: Kyle was such a good student that he figured the application would be just a formality.
sentences.zh: 凯尔是个好学生，他觉得申请流程也就是走个形式。

sentences.en: But he didn't get called back for an interview.
sentences.zh: 但他没有接到面试通知。

sentences.en: His application was red-lighted by the personality test he'd taken when he applied for the job.
sentences.zh: 他的申请在参加工作申请时做的性格测试这一关就被亮了红灯。

sentences.en: The test was part of an employee selection algorithm developed by a private workforce company called Kronos.
sentences.zh: 这个测试是名为克罗诺斯的私营劳动力公司开发的一款员工筛选算法的一部分。

sentences.en: 70% of job applicants in this country take personality tests before they get an interview.
sentences.zh: 这个国家70%的求职者在获得面试机会之前都要参加性格测试。

sentences.en: So this is a very common practice.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种非常普遍的做法。

sentences.en: Kyle had that screening and he found out because his friend worked at Kroger's that he had failed the teSt.
sentences.zh: 凯尔接受了这项筛查，由于他的朋友在克罗格工作，他才发现自己没通过测试。

sentences.en: So most people never find that out.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人永远都不会发现这一点。

sentences.en: They just don't hear back.
sentences.zh: 他们只是收不到回复而已。

sentences.en: And the other thing that was unusual about Kyle is that his dad is a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 关于凯尔，还有一点不寻常的是，他的父亲是一名律师。

sentences.en: So his dad was like, what were the questions like on this test?
sentences.zh: 所以他父亲就问了，这个测试里的问题都是什么样的？

sentences.en: And he said, well, some of them were a lot like the questions I got at the hospital, the mental health assessment.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，其中有些问题很像我在医院里做过的心理健康评估。

sentences.en: The test Kyle got at the hospital was called the five-factor model teSt.
sentences.zh: 凯尔在医院做的那个测试被称为“五因素模型测试”。

sentences.en: And it grades people on extroversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, neuroticism, and openness to new ideas.
sentences.zh: 它从外向性、宜人性、责任心、神经质和对新事物的开放性这几个维度对人进行评分。

sentences.en: It's used in mental health evaluations.
sentences.zh: 它被用于心理健康评估。

sentences.en: The potential employees' answers to the test are then plugged into an algorithm that decides whether the person should be hired.
sentences.zh: 求职者对测试的回答随后会被输入一个算法中，由该算法决定是否应该录用此人。

sentences.en: So his father was like, whoa, that's illegal under the Americans with Disability Act.
sentences.zh: 于是他的父亲就觉得，哇，根据《美国残疾人法案》，这可是非法的。

sentences.en: So his father and he sort of figured out together that something very fishy had been going on.
sentences.zh: 所以他和父亲差不多一起琢磨出，这里面肯定有什么非常可疑的事情。

sentences.en: And his father has actually filed a class-action lawsuit against Kroger's for that.
sentences.zh: 而且他的父亲为此已经对克罗格提起了一起集体诉讼。

sentences.en: The suit is still pending, but arguments are likely to focus on whether the personality test can be considered a medical exam.
sentences.zh: 该诉讼仍在审理中，但辩论的焦点可能在于该性格测试是否可以被视为一项体检。

sentences.en: If it is, it'd be illegal under the ADA.
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，根据《美国残疾人法案》，它就是非法的。

sentences.en: O'Neill gets that different jobs require people with different personality types.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔明白不同的工作需要不同性格类型的人。

sentences.en: But she says a hiring algorithm is a blunt and unregulated tool that ends up disqualifying big categories of people,
sentences.zh: 但她说，招聘算法是一种生硬且不受监管的工具，最终会导致一大批人被直接淘汰，

sentences.en: which makes it a classic weapon of math destruction.
sentences.zh: 这使它成为了一件典型的数学毁灭武器。

sentences.en: In certain jobs, you wouldn't want neurotic people or introverted people.
sentences.zh: 在某些工作中，你不会希望有神经质或性格内向的人。

sentences.en: Like if you're at a call center where a lot of really irate customers call you up, that might be a problem.
sentences.zh: 比如你在一个客服中心，会有很多非常愤怒的客户打电话进来，那可能会是个问题。

sentences.en: In which case, it is actually legal if you get an exception for your company.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，如果你为公司申请了特例，那其实是合法的。

sentences.en: The problem is that these personality tests are not carefully designed for each business.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，这些性格测试并不是针对每家企业精心设计的。

sentences.en: But rather what happens is that these companies just sell the same personality tests to all the businesses that will buy them.
sentences.zh: 实际情况往往是，这些公司把同一套性格测试卖给所有愿意购买它们的商业机构。

sentences.en: A lot of the algorithms that O'Neill explores in her book are largely hidden.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔在书中探讨的许多算法在很大程度上都是隐蔽的。

sentences.en: They don't get a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 它们没有受到太多关注。

sentences.en: We as consumers and job applicants and employees may not even be aware that they're humming along in the background of our lives,
sentences.zh: 作为消费者、求职者和雇员的我们，甚至可能都没有意识到它们正在我们生活的背景中悄悄运转，

sentences.en: sorting us into piles and categories.
sentences.zh: 把我们分门别类地归入各种堆栈和类别中。

sentences.en: But there is one kind of algorithm that's gotten a lot of attention in the news lately.
sentences.zh: 但最近有一种算法在新闻中受到了极大的关注。

sentences.en: Is this a good or bad thing that social media has been able to infiltrate politics?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体能够渗透进政治，这究竟是好是坏？

sentences.en: Social media is a technology.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体是一种技术。

sentences.en: And as we know, technologies have their good sides and their dark sides.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所知，技术都有好的一面和黑暗的一面。

sentences.en: They're not so good sides.
sentences.zh: 也有不那么好的一面。

sentences.en: So it all depends on...
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都取决于……

sentences.en: Towards the end of our conversation, O'Neill and I started talking about the recent election
sentences.zh: 在对话快结束时，我和奥尼尔谈到了最近的选举，

sentences.en: and the complex ways that social media algorithms shape the news that we receive.
sentences.zh: 以及社交媒体算法塑造我们所接收到的新闻的复杂方式。

sentences.en: Facebook shows us stories and ads based on what they think we want.
sentences.zh: 脸书根据它认为我们想要的内容向我们展示故事和广告。

sentences.en: And of course, what they think we want is based on algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 当然，它认为我们想要的正是基于算法。

sentences.en: These algorithms look at what we've clicked on before and then feed us more content we like.
sentences.zh: 这些算法会查看我们以前点击过什么，然后向我们推送更多我们喜欢的内容。

sentences.en: The result is that we've ended up in these information silos,
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我们最终陷入了这些信息茧房中，

sentences.en: increasingly polarized and oblivious to what people of different political persuasions might be seeing.
sentences.zh: 日益走向极端，并且对持不同政治倾向的人可能会看到什么一无所知。

sentences.en: I do think this is a major problem.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是一个大问题。

sentences.en: You know, it's sort of the sky's the limit.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这简直是无上限的。

sentences.en: We have built the internet and the internet is a propaganda machine.
sentences.zh: 我们建立互联网，而互联网就是一个宣传机器。

sentences.en: It's a propaganda, you know, delivery device, if you will.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，它是一个宣传的，你知道的，分发装置。

sentences.en: And that's not...
sentences.zh: 而且那不是……

sentences.en: I don't see how that's going to stop.
sentences.zh: 我看不出这要怎么停下来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Especially if every moment is being optimized by an algorithm that's meant to manipulate your emotions.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当每一个时刻都被旨在操纵你情绪的算法所优化时。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's exactly going back to Facebook's optimizer algorithm.
sentences.zh: 这正是回到脸书的优化算法上去。

sentences.en: That's not optimizing for truth, right?
sentences.zh: 那不是为了真理而优化，对吧？

sentences.en: It's optimizing for profit.
sentences.zh: 它是为了利润而优化。

sentences.en: And they claim to be neutral.
sentences.zh: 而他们声称自己是中立的。

sentences.en: But, of course, nothing's neutral.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，没有什么是中立的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we have seen the results.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了结果。

sentences.en: We've seen what it's actually optimized for.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到它实际上是为了什么进行优化的。

sentences.en: And it's not pretty.
sentences.zh: 而且这并不好看。

sentences.en: This kind of data-driven political microtargeting means conspiracies and misinformation can gain surprising traction online.
sentences.zh: 这种由数据驱动的政治微观定向投放意味着阴谋论和虚假信息可以在网络上获得惊人的影响力。

sentences.en: Stories claiming that Pope Francis endorsed Donald Trump
sentences.zh: 声称教皇方济各支持唐纳德·特朗普的故事，

sentences.en: and that Hillary Clinton sold weapons to ISIS gained millions of viewers on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 以及希拉里·克林顿向伊斯兰国出售武器的故事，在脸书上获得了数百万的浏览量。

sentences.en: Neither of those stories was true.
sentences.zh: 这两个故事都不是真的。

sentences.en: Fixing the problem of these destructive algorithms is not going to be easy.
sentences.zh: 要解决这些具有破坏性的算法所带来的问题并不容易。

sentences.en: Especially when they're insinuating themselves into more and more parts of our lives.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当它们正逐渐渗透到我们生活的越来越多的方面时。

sentences.en: But O'Neill thinks that measurement and transparency is one place to start.
sentences.zh: 但奥尼尔认为，衡量和透明度是一个良好的开端。

sentences.en: Like with that Facebook algorithm and the political ads that it serves to its users.
sentences.zh: 就像脸书的那个算法以及它向用户投放的政治广告一样。

sentences.en: If you were to talk to Facebook about how to inject some ethics into their optimization,
sentences.zh: 如果你要跟脸书谈谈如何在其优化中注入一些伦理道德，

sentences.en: what would you do?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Would you sort of make a case for the bottom line of truth being like a longer tail way to make more money?
sentences.zh: 你会不会为真理的底线辩护，说这是一种能通过长尾效应赚更多钱的方式？

sentences.en: Or would you just say, this is about ethics and you should be thinking about ethics?
sentences.zh: 还是你会直接说，这关乎道德，你们应该考虑一下道德？

sentences.en: To be honest, if I really had their attention, I would ask them to voluntarily find a space on the web
sentences.zh: 说实话，如果我真的能引起他们的注意，我会要求他们自愿在网络上找出一个空间，

sentences.en: to just put every political ad, and actually every ad, just have a way for journalists and people interested in the concept of the informed citizenry
sentences.zh: 把每一个政治广告，甚至实际上是每一个广告都放进去，让记者和对知情公民概念感兴趣的人能够去查阅，

sentences.en: to go through all the ads that they have on Facebook at a given time.
sentences.zh: 只要通过某种方式，就能查看他们在特定时间点于脸书上投放的所有广告。

sentences.en: Because even if that article about Hillary Clinton and ISIS was shared thousands of times,
sentences.zh: 因为即使关于希拉里和伊斯兰国的那个文章被分享了成千上万次，

sentences.en: lots of people never saw it at all.
sentences.zh: 也有很多人根本就没见过它。

sentences.en: Just show us what you're showing other people.
sentences.zh: 只要把你们展示给别人的东西也展示给我们看就行了。

sentences.en: Because I think one of the most pernicious issues is the fact that we don't know what other people are seeing.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为最有害的问题之一，就是我们根本不知道别人都在看什么。

sentences.en: I'm not waiting for Facebook to like actually go against their interests and like change their profit goal.
sentences.zh: 我不指望脸书会真正违背自身的利益去改变他们的利润目标。

sentences.en: But I do think this kind of transparency can be demanded and given.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这种透明度是可以被要求并能够实现的。

sentences.en: O'Neill also says it's important to measure the broad effects of these algorithms and to understand who they most impact.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔还表示，衡量这些算法的广泛影响并了解它们对谁的影响最大，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: Everyone should start measuring it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都应该开始进行衡量。

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is relatively simple.
sentences.zh: 我这么说的意思其实很简单。

sentences.en: And this might not be a complete start, but it's a pretty good first step, which is measure for whom this fails.
sentences.zh: 这可能不是一个完美的开始，但却是一个相当不错的第一步，那就是衡量这对谁来说是失效的。

sentences.en: Meaning which populations are most negatively impacted by the results of these algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 也就是指哪些人群受这些算法结果的负面影响最大。

sentences.en: And what is the harm that befalls those people for whom it fails?
sentences.zh: 对于那些算法对之失效的人来说，他们遭受了什么样的伤害？

sentences.en: And how are the failures distributed across the population?
sentences.zh: 这些失效在整个人群中是如何分布的？

sentences.en: So if you see a hiring algorithm fail much more often for women than for men, that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你发现一个招聘算法对女性失效的频率远高于男性，那就是个问题。

sentences.en: Especially if the failure is they don't get hired when they should get hired.
sentences.zh: 特别是当这种失效表现为她们本来该被录用却没有被录用时。

sentences.en: I really do think that a study, a close examination of the distribution of failures and the harms of those failures would really, really be a good start.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为，对失效的分布及其带来的伤害进行研究和密切审查，绝对、绝对会是一个很好的开端。

sentences.en: If you're not mad enough about how algorithms influence your life, I've got a doozy for you after these messages.
sentences.zh: 如果你对算法如何影响你的生活还不够愤怒，在这些广告之后，我有一个重磅消息要告诉你。

sentences.en: We are currently experiencing higher call volumes than normal.
sentences.zh: 我们目前的客服呼叫量高于平常。

sentences.en: Please stay on the line and an agent will be with you shortly.
sentences.zh: 请不要挂机，稍后会有客服代表为您服务。

sentences.en: Here's one that I think is kind of fun because it's annoying and secret, but you would never know it.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个我觉得挺有意思的例子，因为它既讨厌又隐蔽，但你永远不会察觉到。

sentences.en: So if you call up a customer service line, I'm not saying this will always happen, but it will sometimes happen,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你拨打客服热线，我不是说这种情况一定会发生，但有时确实会发生，

sentences.en: that your phone number will be used to backtrack who you are.
sentences.zh: 你的电话号码会被用来通过回溯来确定你的身份。

sentences.en: You will be sussed as, like, are you a high-value customer or a low-value customer?
sentences.zh: 你会被甄别，比如，你是有价值的高端客户还是低价值客户？

sentences.en: And if you're a high-value customer, you'll talk to a customer service representative much sooner than if you're a low-value customer.
sentences.zh: 如果你是高端客户，你与客服代表对话的速度会比低端客户快得多。

sentences.en: You'll be put on hold longer.
sentences.zh: 你会面临更长时间的等待。

sentences.en: That's how businesses make decisions nowadays.
sentences.zh: 这就是当今企业做出决策的方式。

sentences.en: You are caller number 99.
sentences.zh: 您是第99位来电者。

sentences.en: Your call is important to us.
sentences.zh: 您的来电对我们很重要。

sentences.en: Please stay on the line.
sentences.zh: 请保持在线。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由德兰妮·霍尔制作。

sentences.en: Tech and mixed production by Emmett Fitzgerald.
sentences.zh: 技术和混音制作由埃米特·菲茨杰拉德负责。

sentences.en: Katie Mingle is the senior producer.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂·明格是高级制作人。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is the digital director.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯塔德是数字总监。

sentences.en: Sean Rial composed all the music.
sentences.zh: 肖恩·里亚尔创作了所有的音乐。

sentences.en: The rest of the staff includes Avery Truffleman, Sharif Youssef, Taryn Mazza, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 其他工作人员包括艾弗里·特鲁夫曼、谢里夫·优素福、塔琳·马扎，以及我，罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Ryan Kiesler and Courtney Riddle.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢瑞安·基斯勒和考特尼·里德尔。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 KALW in San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，在美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心电台街制作。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is part of Radiotopia from PRX, a collective of the best, most innovative shows in all of podcasting.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》是 PRX 旗下 Radiotopia 的一部分，这是一个汇集了播客界最优秀、最具创新性节目的联盟。

sentences.en: We are supported by the Knight Foundation and coin-carrying listeners just like you.
sentences.zh: 我们的资金支持来自奈特基金会和像你这样随身带着硬币的听众。

sentences.en: You can find 99% Invisible and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在脸书上找到《99%隐形》并加入关于节目的讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me, at Roman Mars, and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上@我（@Roman Mars），也可以在 99pi.org 关注节目。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram, Tumblr, and Reddit, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram、Tumblr 和 Reddit 上。

sentences.en: But our lovely home on the internet with more design stories than we can ever tell you here on the radio,
sentences.zh: 但我们在互联网上的可爱家园，拥有比我们在广播中，

sentences.en: or podcast, I guess this is a podcast,
sentences.zh: 或者说播客中——我想这是一个播客——所能讲述的更多的设计故事，

sentences.en: is our website at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 就是我们的网站 99pi.org。

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
